text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"rent_increase_limits","status":"in_force","title":"California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act rent limits, SB 567 version)","requirement":"An owner of residential real property may not, over any 12-month period, raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. The base is the lowest gross rental rate charged for the unit at any time in the 12 months before the increase takes effect, excluding discounts, incentives, concessions or credits the tenant accepted. If the same tenant stays in occupancy, there may be no more than two increases in any 12-month period. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession. A tenant may not sublease for a total rent above the allowable rate. Increase notices must follow Civ. Code § 827. Waivers are void. The cost-of-living change is the CPI-U percentage change for the applicable metropolitan area (April-to-April, with a March fallback), rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent.","key_value":"5% + local CPI change, capped at 10% (whichever is lower), per 12 months; max two increases per 12 months","coverage_conditions":"Applies to residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in mobilehome parks) statewide. Mobilehome tenancies are covered only for increases on or after 2021-02-18; other housing for increases on or after 2019-03-15. The section does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome.","exemptions":"(1) Deed-restricted or regulatory-restricted affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income households, or housing subject to an affordable-housing subsidy agreement. (2) Dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school. (3) Housing subject to a valid local rent or price control that limits annual increases to less than the state cap. (4) Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (not applicable to mobilehomes). (5) Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit (including a mobilehome), if the owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, and tenants received the required written exemption notice.
